newsitem.title: GERMANY: Prague sees German pact ready, waits for Bonn.
newsitem.headline: Prague sees German pact ready, waits for Bonn.

text.p: A long-awaited reconciliation pact between Germany and the Czech Republic is ready for signing as far as Prague is concerned, Czech Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec said in an interview published on Tuesday.
The text to resolve the last major World War Two dispute between Germany and one of its neighbours just required approval from Bonn, Zieleniec told the Frankfurter Rundschau newspaper.
"We think the text is finished," he said. "I believe the search for approval of the finished text is more of a domestic German debate."

He added: "Many politicians have said a lot over the past few years about how the declaration should look. Now they're bringing their comments into line with the reality presented by the provisional text."
The agreement is expected to regulate issues of property and compensation for both Czech victims of Nazi aggression and for millions of ethnic Germans driven out of Czechoslovakia.
Chancellor Helmut Kohl said last month he hoped the declaration could be signed this year.

But Kohl's coalition allies, the Bavarian Christian Social Union (CSU), have consistently championed the cause of the 2.5 million ethnic "Sudeten Germans" forced to leave after the war and demanded Prague negotiate directly with expellees' groups.

Zieleniec told the Frankfurter Rundschau Prague would stick to its position of only dealing with Bonn. "This is a basic issue. The Czech government represents the Czech people and the German government represents the German people," he said.
